fact: Plasmodium vivax relapse infections occur when latent liver-stage parasites, called hypnozoites, activate, causing new blood-stage infections weeks to months after the initial infection.
source_span: Plasmodium vivax relapse infections occur following activation of latent liver-stages parasites ( hypnozoites ) causing new blood-stage infections weeks to months after the initial infection .
abstract_sentence: Plasmodium vivax relapse infections occur following activation of latent liver-stages parasites (hypnozoites) causing new blood-stage infections weeks to months after the initial infection.

fact: A within-host mathematical model of liver-stage hypnozoites was developed and validated against data from tropical strains of P. vivax.
source_span: We develop a within-host mathematical model of liver-stage hypnozoites , and validate it against data from tropical strains of P . vivax . In this manuscript , a within-host model of hypnozoites in liver hepatocytes is developed to demonstrate that many of the epidemiological patterns of relapse infections can be explained by making the assumption that hypnozoites activate and die at a constant rate .
abstract_sentence: We develop a within-host mathematical model of liver-stage hypnozoites, and validate it against data from tropical strains of P. vivax.

fact: The within-host relapse model was fitted to data on time to first relapse infection from three ecological zones: South America, South East Asia, and Melanesia.
source_span: Figure 1 shows the best fit within-host relapse model to data on time to first relapse infection from three ecological zones with tropical strains of P . vivax: South America , South East Asia and Melanesia ( Battle et al . , 2014 ) .
abstract_sentence: We develop a within-host mathematical model of liver-stage hypnozoites, and validate it against data from tropical strains of P. vivax.

fact: The within-host model was integrated into a P. vivax transmission model to show how the hypnozoite reservoir builds up after new infections and depletes through activation and death.
source_span: The within-host model is embedded in a P . vivax transmission model to demonstrate the build-up of the hypnozoite reservoir following new infections and its depletion through hypnozoite activation and death . We next embedded the within-host model for tropical relapses in a model for the transmission of P . vivax between humans and mosquitoes ( Figure 8 ) . Following infection with a tropical strain of P . vivax , the population dynamics of hypnozoites in the liver can be described by a within-host model where each hypnozoite is subject to two processes: ( i ) activation leading to relapse infection; and ( ii ) death , either of the hypnozoite itself or the host hepatocyte ( Malato et al . , 2011 ) .
abstract_sentence: The within-host model is embedded in a P. vivax transmission model to demonstrate the build-up of the hypnozoite reservoir following new infections and its depletion through hypnozoite activation and death.

fact: The model predicts that the hypnozoite reservoir is over-dispersed, meaning many individuals have few or no hypnozoites, while some have intensely infected livers.
source_span: The hypnozoite reservoir is predicted to be over-dispersed with many individuals having few or no hypnozoites , and some having intensely infected livers . The number of hypnozoites per individual is predicted to be over-dispersed following a negative binomial distribution . Thus some individuals will harbour a large number of hypnozoites while some will have none .
abstract_sentence: The hypnozoite reservoir is predicted to be over-dispersed with many individuals having few or no hypnozoites, and some having intensely infected livers.

fact: The model predicts that individuals with more hypnozoites will experience more relapses and contribute more to the onward transmission of P. vivax.
source_span: Individuals with more hypnozoites are predicted to experience more relapses and contribute more to onwards P . vivax transmission . This model predicts notable dose-dependency with increased numbers of hypnozoites associated with a greater number of relapses and shorter time to first relapse .
abstract_sentence: Individuals with more hypnozoites are predicted to experience more relapses and contribute more to onwards P. vivax transmission.

fact: Incorporating hypnozoite-killing drugs like primaquine into first-line treatment regimens is predicted to cause substantial reductions in P. vivax transmission.
source_span: Incorporating hypnozoite killing drugs such as primaquine into first-line treatment regimens is predicted to cause substantial reductions in P . vivax transmission as individuals with the most hypnozoites are more likely to relapse and be targeted for treatment . The inclusion of primaquine in first-line treatment regimens is predicted to cause substantial reductions in both the P . vivax parasite rate and hypnozoite rate ( Figure 5C ) , as individuals being treated for blood-stage P . vivax infections will also have their hypnozoites removed . A consequence of this strategy is that the hypnozoite reservoir can be targeted efficiently , as individuals with the most hypnozoites are most likely to relapse and potentially be detected by health systems .
abstract_sentence: Incorporating hypnozoite killing drugs such as primaquine into first-line treatment regimens is predicted to cause substantial reductions in P. vivax transmission as individuals with the most hypnozoites are more likely to relapse and be targeted for treatment.

fact: The hypnozoite reservoir can be directly targeted using drugs like primaquine, which eliminate hypnozoites from the liver.
source_span: The hypnozoite reservoir can be directly targeted using a drug such as primaquine that can eliminate hypnozoites from the liver ( Wells et al . , 2010 ) .
abstract_sentence: Incorporating hypnozoite killing drugs such as primaquine into first-line treatment regimens is predicted to cause substantial reductions in P. vivax transmission as individuals with the most hypnozoites are more likely to relapse and be targeted for treatment.

source_span: When 2 Mha of Amazonian forests are disturbed by selective logging each year , more than 90 Tg of carbon ( C ) is emitted to the atmosphere . Among those disturbances , selective logging , i . e . the selective harvest of a few merchantable tree species , is particularly widespread: in the Brazilian Amazon alone , about 2 Mha yr−1 were logged in 1999–2002 ( Asner et al . , 2005 ) .

fact: The study utilized an original modeling approach, calibrated on a network of 133 permanent forest plots (175 ha total) across Amazonia, to provide Amazon-wide predictions of post-logging carbon recovery.
source_span: With an original modelling approach , calibrated on a network of 133 permanent forest plots ( 175 ha total ) across Amazonia , we link regional differences in climate , soil and initial biomass with survivors’ and recruits’ C fluxes to provide Amazon-wide predictions of post-logging C recovery . Based on long-term ( 8–30 year ) inventory data from 13 experimentally-disturbed sites ( Sist et al . , 2015 ) across Amazonia ( Figure 1—figure supplement 1 ) , 133 permanent forest plots ( 175 ha in total ) that cover a large gradient of disturbance intensities ( ACS losses ranging from 1% to 71% ) were used to model the trajectory of those post-disturbance ACS changes ( Figure 1 ) in a comprehensive Bayesian framework .

source_span: To test these predictions , we introduce a novel sensory manipulation that mimics the addition of unbiased noise to motion-selective regions of visual cortex, which we verified with neuronal recordings from macaque areas MT/MST . To test these predictions , we introduce a novel sensory manipulation that mimics the addition of unbiased noise to motion-selective regions of visual cortex , which we verified with neuronal recordings from macaque areas MT/MST . We achieved this with a manipulation of the motion information in a random dot motion ( RDM ) display , by adding a second level of randomness which increased its volatility but was unbiased with respect to the strength and direction of motion evidence . fact: The nervous system's implementation of motor sequence formation, through the serial execution of different movements, is largely unknown.
source_span: Motor sequences are formed through the serial execution of different movements , but how nervous systems implement this process remains largely unknown . Grooming consists of discrete cleaning movements that occur in predictable sequences; however , the mechanisms that govern transitions between the movements are not known ( Szebenyi , 1969; Fentress and Stilwell , 1973; Dawkins and Dawkins , 1976; Sachs , 1988 ) .
abstract_sentence: How nervous systems implement the serial execution of different movements to form motor sequences is largely unknown.

fact: The motor programs for grooming in fruit flies are organized into a suppression hierarchy, where programs occurring first suppress those that occur later.
source_span: This enabled competition experiments revealing that the motor programs are organized into a suppression hierarchy; motor programs that occur first suppress those that occur later . For this hypothesis to account for the fly grooming progression , the order of suppression within the hierarchy would have to match the order of the normal grooming sequence , as schematized ( Figure 3A ) .
abstract_sentence: Competition experiments revealed that motor programs are organized into a suppression hierarchy, where earlier programs suppress later ones.

fact: Cleaning one body part reduces the sensory drive to its motor program, which then relieves suppression of the next movement, allowing the grooming sequence to progress down the hierarchy.
source_span: Cleaning one body part reduces the sensory drive to its motor program , which relieves suppression of the next movement , allowing the grooming sequence to progress down the hierarchy . Once a module is selected, the reduced sensory drive that results from cleaning dust from the relevant body part gradually lowers its activation level, thereby allowing cleaning to proceed to whichever module has the next highest activation level (In Figure 4A, the removal of dust by a module is represented with blunt arrows from the winner-take-all layer to the dust). In grooming , the active module ‘deletes’ itself from the sequence by reducing the dust stimulated sensory drive through cleaning

fact: Affected motor neurons in Fz3-deficient organisms die two days before the normal developmental cell death wave that occurs when muscles are innervated.

fact: The results provide evidence that neurons in the macaque entorhinal cortex do not rely on physical movement for their spatial representations.

fact: The phase of the circadian rhythm in cyanobacteria follows a simple scaling law in light-dark cycles, tracking midday across conditions with variable day length.
source_span: We find that the phase of the circadian rhythm follows a simple scaling law in light-dark cycles , tracking midday across conditions with variable day length . source_span: Imaging of sporozoites with mutations in key adhesive proteins highlight the importance of the sporozoite's gliding speed and its ability to modulate adhesive properties for successful exit from the inoculation site . The importance of high sporozoite gliding speed is highlighted by the behavior of the TRAP-VAL mutant that moves with less than half the motile speed of wild-type control parasites in the dermis . This decrease in speed corresponds to the reduction of final MSD , which reduces the area of tissue explored by 70% . Consequently , TRAP-VAL sporozoites have a significantly decreased chance to encounter and invade a blood vessel , which together with the increase in number of non-motile TRAP-VAL sporozoites , largely explains their reduced infectivity ( Ejigiri et al . , 2012 ) . Our data with both TRAP-VAL and CSΔN mutant sporozoites demonstrate that the sporozoite's ability to regulate its adhesive intereactions is a key factor for successful movement through and out of the dermis. fact: It remains unclear whether the denervation of neuromuscular junctions (NMJ) in ALS is simply the first manifestation of a globally degenerating motor neuron or arises from local branch-specific degeneration.
source_span: Despite being an early event in ALS , it remains unclear whether the denervation of neuromuscular junctions ( NMJ ) is simply the first manifestation of a globally degenerating motor neuron . However , whether early NMJ denervation arises from local branch-specific degeneration ( ‘dying-back hypothesis’ ) or is merely the manifestation of a diseased and globally degenerating motor neuron remains ill-defined . Denervation of NMJs is observed prior to symptom onset ( Clark et al . , 2016; Fischer et al . , 2004; Pun et al . , 2006; Tallon et al . , 2016; Vinsant et al . , 2013 ) and before any significant MN axonal or cell body loss ( Fischer et al . , 2004; Vinsant et al . , 2013 ) . Loss of neuromuscular junctions ( NMJs ) is a key pathological event in ALS patients ( Fischer et al . , 2004; Killian et al . , 1994 ) and in animal models of the disease ( Clark et al . , 2016; Fischer et al . , 2004; Frey et al . , 2000; Pun et al . , 2006; Tallon et al . , 2016 ) .

source_span: Denervation events tend to propagate from the first lost NMJ , consistent with a contribution of neuromuscular factors extrinsic to motor neurons , with distal branches being more susceptible . Indeed , NMJs arising from distal axonal branches were more susceptible to being lost ( Figure 4D , red dots , 38 events , n = 253 , N = 11 , logistic regression , p=0 . 010 ) , while MU expansions were more likely to occur on proximal branches ( mainly first-order branches ) ( Figure 4D , blue dots , 76 events , n = 253 , N = 11 , logistic regression , p=0 . 001 ) . These results unravel a propagation pattern and suggest that factors extrinsic to motor axons ( i . e . the local neuromuscular environment ) interact with the intrinsic properties of motor axons ( e . g . susceptibility of specific branches ) , to shape the pattern of NMJ loss in ALS .

Altogether , these results show that rather than being exclusively degenerating or compensating , MUs are highly dynamic during disease progression , with specific branches either expanding or disassembling . fact: Single-molecule Förster Resonance energy transfer (smFRET) is a method used to study the structure and dynamics of biomolecules.
source_span: Single-molecule Förster Resonance energy transfer ( smFRET ) is an adaptable method for studying the structure and dynamics of biomolecules . Capturing the real-time readouts of nanometer-scale distances of individual biomolecules by smFRET allows the direct observations of dynamics , interactions , and intermediates of stochastic non-accumulating events , as well as dynamic equilibria between unsynchronized molecules , all of which are obscured in ensemble averaging techniques ( Dimura et al . , 2016; Hellenkamp et al . , 2018; Holmstrom et al . , 2019; Juette et al . , 2016; Newton et al . , 2019; Preus et al . , 2015; Roy et al . , 2008; Schuler and Eaton , 2008; Stella et al . , 2018 ) .
abstract_sentence: Single-molecule Förster Resonance energy transfer (smFRET) is an adaptable method for studying the structure and dynamics of biomolecules.

fact: The development of high-throughput smFRET methodologies and commercial instrumentation has outpaced the development of rapid, standardized, and automated data analysis methods.
source_span: The development of high throughput methodologies and the growth of commercial instrumentation have outpaced the development of rapid , standardized , and automated methodologies to objectively analyze the wealth of produced data . Existing software ( Greenfeld et al . , 2012; Hellenkamp et al . , 2018; Hon and Gonzalez , 2019; Juette et al . , 2016; Preus et al . , 2015; Stella et al . , 2018 ) by single-molecule labs can simplify the tedious and time-consuming selection of traces and were recently expanded to large datasets ( Juette et al . , 2016 ) albeit requiring some form of manual supervision and hyper-parameter tuning selecting the proper thresholds by an expert user . This need for human intervention could potentially be subjected to cognitive biases especially by less experienced users and could limit the expansion of smFRET to classic biology labs .
abstract_sentence: The development of high throughput methodologies and the growth of commercial instrumentation have outpaced the development of rapid, standardized, and automated methodologies to objectively analyze the wealth of produced data.

source_span: Asymptomatic carriage in the nasopharynx is a prerequisite for disease , but variability in its duration is currently only understood at the serotype level . One factor that is known to strongly associate with carriage duration is serotype: as capsular polysaccharides are important in bacterial physiology and determining host immune response , different serotypes have different clearance and acquisition rates ( Abdullahi et al . , 2012a; Hill et al . , 2010; Högberg et al . , 2007; Melegaro et al . , 2004; Turner et al . , 2012 ) . For 598 unvaccinated children up to 24 swabs taken over a two year period were available , an extension on the previous study ( Turner et al . , 2012 , 2013a ) . To estimate carriage duration from the longitudinal swab data we constructed a set of hidden Markov models ( HMMs ) with hidden states corresponding to whether a child was carrying a serotype at a given time point , and observed states corresponding to whether a positive swab was observed for this serotype at this time point .

fact: APOBEC3A (A3A) is the most powerful inhibitor of L1 retrotransposition in lab cell tests.
source_span: Among these enzymes , APOBEC3A ( A3A ) is the most potent inhibitor of L1 retrotransposition in cultured cell assays . Previous studies revealed that over-expression of the wild-type ( WT ) APOBEC3A cytidine deaminase protein ( A3A ) , but not deaminase-defective A3A mutants , could potently inhibit L1 retrotransposition in cultured human cells ( Chen et al . , 2006; Muckenfuss et al . , 2006; Bogerd et al . , 2006b; Kinomoto et al . , 2007; Niewiadomska et al . , 2007 ) . Together , these experiments show that A3A inhibits retrotransposition of diverse LINE elements in cultured cells .
abstract_sentence: Among these enzymes, APOBEC3A (A3A) is the most potent inhibitor of L1 retrotransposition in cultured cell assays.

fact: However, deamination events were not found in L1 retrotransposition when wild-type APOBEC3A (A3A) was present.
source_span: However , deamination events were not detected in L1 retrotransposition events generated in the presence of WT A3A ( Chen et al . , 2006; Muckenfuss et al . , 2006; Bogerd et al . , 2006b; Kinomoto et al . , 2007 ) . Such a scenario could explain why previous studies failed to detect A3A-mediated deamination events in engineered L1 retrotransposition events ( Chen et al . , 2006; Muckenfuss et al . , 2006; Bogerd et al . , 2006b; Kinomoto et al . , 2007 ) .
abstract_sentence: However, previous characterization of L1 retrotransposition events generated in the presence of A3A did not yield evidence of deamination.

fact: This study used in vitro and in vivo tests to show that APOBEC3A (A3A) can stop L1 retrotransposition by changing single-strand DNA that is temporarily exposed during L1 integration.
source_span: Here , we have used in vitro and in vivo assays to demonstrate that A3A can inhibit L1 retrotransposition by deaminating transiently exposed single-strand DNA that arises during the process of L1 integration . Here , we employ an in vitro assay ( L1 Element Amplification Protocol or LEAP ) that recapitulates the first strand cDNA synthesis step of the L1 integration to elucidate a mechanism for A3A-mediated inhibition of L1 retrotransposition . In LEAP reactions that include RNase H , an enzyme that specifically degrades the RNA strand of an RNA/DNA heteroduplex , we report that single-strand L1 cDNAs are rendered susceptible to A3A-mediated deamination . We therefore hypothesized that A3A may deaminate transiently exposed single-strand DNA intermediates that arise during L1 TPRT in cultured cells .

fact: Participants select eye movements with the goal of maximizing information about abstract categories.
source_span: Our results suggest that participants select eye movements with the goal of maximizing information about abstract categories that require the integration of information from multiple locations. Second , by using a pattern categorization task we could ensure that no single location was especially informative but that the task required an integration of information from multiple locations both to select the next eye movement and to solve the task , and specifically that a closed-loop strategy was necessary for solving the task efficiently .

fact: Lab-infected Drosophila melanogaster flies exhibit characteristic moribund behaviors due to Entomophthora muscae infection, including climbing upward, affixing themselves, and raising their wings for spore dispersal.
source_span: Lab-infected flies manifest the moribund behaviors characteristic of E . muscae infection: hours before death , they climb upward , extend their proboscides , affixing in place , then raise their wings , clearing a path for infectious spores to launch from their abdomens . A fly infected with E . muscae exhibits a characteristic set of fungus-induced behaviors: shortly before sunset on its final day of life , the fly climbs to a high location ( a behavior known as ‘summiting’ ) , extends its proboscis and becomes affixed to the surface via fungal holdfasts , hyphal growths that emerge through the mouthparts ( Roy et al . , 2006; Balazy , 1984; Krasnoff et al . , 1995 ) . The fly’s wings then lift up and away from its dorsal abdomen , striking a final death pose that is thought to be ideal for fungal dispersal ( Krasnoff et al . , 1995 ) .

fact: The study found that when beta oscillations were present, whether induced by neurofeedback or occurring naturally, the overall activity of neuron populations moved further away from the patterns typically seen at the start of movement.

While antimalarials are usually administered following diagnosis ( confirmed or presumed ) or used as a prophylactic , MDA is used because of an intended population- or community-level effect . fact: The roles of chance, contingency, and necessity in evolution are unresolved because they have never been assessed in a single system or on timescales relevant to historical evolution.
source_span: The roles of chance , contingency , and necessity in evolution are unresolved because they have never been assessed in a single system or on timescales relevant to historical evolution . fact: Chance arose because many sets of mutations could alter specificity at any timepoint.
source_span: Chance arose because many sets of mutations could alter specificity at any timepoint contingency arose because historical substitutions changed these sets . fact: The association between nucleosome footprints and sequence evolution is strikingly conserved between humans and Haloferax volcanii.
source_span: Here , we show that despite these fundamental differences the association between nucleosome footprints and sequence evolution is strikingly conserved between humans and the model archaeon Haloferax volcanii . Here , we demonstrate that – despite such differences in nucleosome structure , global nucleotide substitution profiles and general cellular physiology – nucleosome-associated substitution patterns along the Hfx . volcanii lineage are remarkably similar to those observed in humans ( as well as in Drosophila melanogaster ) . Our analysis revealed that substitution patterns in and around nucleosome footprints are remarkably similar along the Hfx . volcanii and human branches , with substitution rates consistently reduced for some ( e . g . C:G to T:A ) but elevated for other ( e . g . A:T to G:C ) base changes when approaching the dyad . These shared biases are observed despite radical differences in global substitution dynamics and structural differences between the histone complexes involved .

fact: Neither the mutation nor the selection model are sufficient to explain the observed association between nucleosomes and sequence divergence.
source_span: Unexpectedly , we find that neither the mutation nor the selection model are sufficient to explain the observed association between nucleosomes and sequence divergence . What our findings do suggest , however , is that mutation/selection biases are not sufficient to explain the observed association between nucleosome positions and nucleotide substitution patterns between species and must operate , if they do , on a background of nucleosome repositioning . We go on to show that these dyad-oriented trends break down in the respective sister lineages , an observation that is neither consistent with mutation nor purifying selection acting on nucleosomes that are positionally static over evolutionary time .
abstract_sentence: Neither the mutation nor the selection model alone can sufficiently explain the observed association between nucleosomes and sequence divergence.

fact: Nucleosome-associated substitution patterns are more consistent with a model where sequence divergence results in frequent repositioning of nucleosomes during evolution.
source_span: Instead , we demonstrate that nucleosome-associated substitution patterns are more consistent with a third model where sequence divergence results in frequent repositioning of nucleosomes during evolution . Instead , we show that these patterns are consistent with widespread local repositioning of nucleosomes in response to substitutions . In contrast , our model of sequence-biased repositioning , which postulates a causal link between sequence change and nucleosome repositioning , does predict a ) concordant trends in the focal lineages across clades , b ) an absence of trends in the sister lineages , and c ) neatly accounts for why we see GC-enriching changes enriched near the dyad ( the nucleosome moved there ) and GC-depleting changes enriched further away from the dyad ( the nucleosome moved away ) .
abstract_sentence: Nucleosome-associated substitution patterns are more consistent with a model where sequence divergence leads to frequent repositioning of nucleosomes during evolution.

fact: Nucleosome repositioning is necessary and largely sufficient to explain the association between current nucleosome positions and biased substitution patterns.
source_span: Indeed , we show that nucleosome repositioning is both necessary and largely sufficient to explain the association between current nucleosome positions and biased substitution patterns . They do , however , strongly suggest that repositioning is necessary and also appears largely sufficient to explain the substitution trends we observe ( see Discussion ) . Further , we argue that biased repositioning is largely sufficient to explain the association between nucleosome topology and nucleotide substitution rates , whereby nucleosomes shift ( likely locally ) from their ancestral position in response to a change in the underlying sequence , and do so in line with known histone binding preferences .
abstract_sentence: Nucleosome repositioning is both necessary and largely sufficient to explain the association between current nucleosome positions and biased substitution patterns.

However , is defined only for idealized discrete Markovian systems ( a Markovian system is one for which the future depends only on the present , and not on the past ) . This in-principle restriction severely limits its in-practice applicability because complex biological systems are typically continuous ( or are measured as continuous ) and are non-Markovian ) . This limitation in turn imposes a serious obstacle for developing and evaluating theories , such as the IITC , which depend on quantifying integrated information .

fact: YKU80 and TLC1 were validated as telomere-length QTLs in two S. paradoxus subpopulations using reciprocal hemizygosity.
source_span: We validated by reciprocal hemizygosity that YKU80 and TLC1 are telomere-length QTLs in the two S . paradoxus subpopulations . We confirmed that part of the variation in telomere length among individuals is due to natural sequence variants within YKU80 and TLC1 . The segregant analysis suggested that the YKU80 marker was strongly linked with the telomere length phenotype ( LOD 5 . 34 , variance explained 12% ) with length averages of 370 bp and 276 bp for the spores carrying the YPS or the CBS allele respectively ( Table S2 ) . Similarly , we validated the quantitative effect on telomere length of TLC1 ( LOD 4 . 25 , variance explained 9 . 74% ) by reciprocal hemizygosity ( Figure 5B ) .

fact: Macrophages need to be activated to efficiently clear infectious pathogens, but how this activation leads to increased clearance is largely unknown.
source_span: Following an infectious challenge , macrophages have to be activated in order to allow efficient clearance of infectious pathogens , but how macrophage activation is coupled to increased clearance remains largely unknown . Macrophages are the main scavengers responsible for clearance of solutes and particulate material as well as to act as defense cells against invading microbes [1] .
abstract_sentence: Macrophages must be activated to efficiently clear infectious pathogens, but the coupling mechanism remains largely unknown.

fact: Inflammatory stimuli reprogram macrophages to switch their uptake method from receptor-mediated phagocytosis to macropinocytosis, which allows rapid, receptor-independent transfer of internalized cargo to lysosomes.
source_span: We here describe that inflammatory stimuli induced the reprogramming of the macrophage endocytic machinery from receptor-mediated phagocytosis to macropinocytosis , allowing the rapid transfer of internalized cargo to lysosomes in a receptor-independent manner . As an alternative to receptor-mediated phagocytosis , macrophages can also internalize material via macropinocytosis , a non-saturable mode of uptake that allows the internalization of large amounts of cargo independent of any receptor usage [11] , [13]–[15] .
abstract_sentence: Inflammatory stimuli reprogram macrophage endocytosis from receptor-mediated phagocytosis to macropinocytosis, allowing rapid, receptor-independent cargo transfer to lysosomes.

fact: The reprogramming from phagocytosis to macropinocytosis happens when protein kinase C phosphorylates the macrophage protein coronin 1, which then activates phosphoinositol (PI)-3-kinase, a key enzyme for macropinocytic uptake.
source_span: Reprogramming occurred through protein kinase C-mediated phosphorylation of the macrophage protein coronin 1 , thereby activating phosphoinositol ( PI ) -3-kinase activity necessary for macropinocytic uptake . Macropinocytosis is crucially dependent on the activation of the lipid kinase phosphoinositide 3-kinase ( PI-3 kinase [17] , [33] ) .
abstract_sentence: This reprogramming occurs through protein kinase C-mediated phosphorylation of coronin 1, which activates PI-3-kinase activity necessary for macropinocytic uptake.

abstract_sentence: Expression of a phosphomimetic form of coronin 1 was sufficient to induce PI3-kinase activation and macropinocytosis even without inflammatory stimuli.

fact: Proteins often perform their biological functions through collective atomic motions.

fact: Identifying collective motions related to a specific protein function from molecular dynamics trajectories is often difficult.
source_span: Yet the identification of collective motions related to a specific protein function from , e . g . , a molecular dynamics trajectory is often non-trivial . abstract_sentence: Identifying collective motions related to a specific protein function from molecular dynamics trajectories is often non-trivial.

fact: The authors propose a new technique called 'functional mode analysis' (FMA) to detect collective motion directly related to a particular protein function.
source_span: Here , we propose a novel technique termed “functional mode analysis” that aims to detect the collective motion that is directly related to a particular protein function . We have presented a novel analysis technique termed functional mode analysis ( FMA ) to systematically identify functionally relevant collective motions in proteins dynamics .
abstract_sentence: Here, we propose a novel technique termed “functional mode analysis” that aims to detect the collective motion that is directly related to a particular protein function.

fact: Functional mode analysis (FMA) uses an ensemble of protein structures and a 'functional quantity' that describes the protein's functional state to detect the collective motion maximally correlated to this quantity.
source_span: Based on an ensemble of structures , together with an arbitrary “functional quantity” that quantifies the functional state of the protein , the technique detects the collective motion that is maximally correlated to the functional quantity . Given that input , the technique seeks the collective protein motion that is maximally related to the functional quantity . In other words , the technique aims to explain variations in the functional quantity in terms of collective motions .
abstract_sentence: Based on an ensemble of structures, together with an arbitrary “functional quantity” that quantifies the functional state of the protein, the technique detects the collective motion that is maximally correlated to the functional quantity.

fact: The 'functional quantity' can be a geometric, electrostatic, or chemical observable, or any other variable relevant to protein function.
source_span: The functional quantity could , e . g . , correspond to a geometric , electrostatic , or chemical observable , or any other variable that is relevant to the function of the protein .
abstract_sentence: The functional quantity could, e.g., correspond to a geometric, electrostatic, or chemical observable, or any other variable that is relevant to the function of the protein.

fact: FMA also estimates the motion most likely to cause a substantial change in the functional quantity, considering the protein's energy landscape.
source_span: In addition , the motion that displays the largest likelihood to induce a substantial change in the functional quantity is estimated from the given protein ensemble . Second , the physical motion that actually accomplishes substantial deviations in , in accordance with the protein's energy landscape , is frequently of interest . Because many different motions might affect , we use the input structure ensemble to estimate the most probable collective motion that accomplishes a substantial change in . That motion will be referred to as ensemble-weighted MCM ( ewMCM ) .
abstract_sentence: In addition, the motion that displays the largest likelihood to induce a substantial change in the functional quantity is estimated from the given protein ensemble.

fact: FMA applies two correlation measures: Pearson correlation coefficient for linear correlation and mutual information for any kind of interdependence, including non-linear.
source_span: Two different correlation measures are applied: first , the Pearson correlation coefficient that measures linear correlation only; and second , the mutual information that can assess any kind of interdependence . We have used two different measures to quantify the correlation between and the collective motion . ( i ) , the Pearson coefficient which measures linear correlation only , and ( ii ) , the mutual information ( MI ) which can assess any kind of correlation including non-linear and higher order correlation .
abstract_sentence: Two different correlation measures are applied: first, the Pearson correlation coefficient that measures linear correlation only; and second, the mutual information that can assess any kind of interdependence.

fact: The polyproline regions form polyproline type II helices, which decrease the likelihood of the polyQ region forming a β-rich state.

Experimental studies of these models , indicate that the polyP regions form polyproline type II ( PPII ) helices [3] , [40] , [41] , which compete with the β-sheet structure of the polyQ region [40] and possibly protect against aggregation [1] , [3] , [5] , [20] , [39] , [40] , [42]–[44] . fact: There is currently no direct genetic evidence to support the foundational model that suberin forms a chemical barrier limiting extracellular transport of water and solutes in plant roots.

A long held model to explain this regulation includes the function of the extracellular biopolymer suberin acting as a barrier to limit the apoplastic transport of water and solutes . fact: The scientific literature, especially in molecular biomedicine, is rapidly expanding, making it challenging for researchers to navigate.
source_span: The profusion of high-throughput instruments and the explosion of new results in the scientific literature , particularly in molecular biomedicine , is both a blessing and a curse to the bench researcher . High-throughput ( also known as genome-scale ) assays for detection and analysis of gene expression , genetic polymorphisms , macromolecular interactions and other fundamental processes are generating datasets that contain information about the structures or activities of on the order of 106 different genes or gene products at a time . The amount of information regarding even just these significant results ( and relevant homologs ) in gene-centric databases and in the research literature is often overwhelming , yet the proper interpretation of the results requires taking stock of all of that knowledge .
abstract_sentence: The rapid growth of scientific literature and high-throughput instruments presents challenges for biomedical researchers.

fact: Reasoning methods enrich the knowledge that results from reading by, for example, noting two genes that are annotated to the same ontology term or database entry.
source_span: An important method for adding semantic relations between genes is to infer that such a relationship exists when two genes have certain properties in common . A series of experts asserts semantic relationships between pairs of genes based on: shared membership in a signaling or metabolic pathway ( co-KEGG ) [34] , shared annotation to a particular biological process ( co-BP ) , molecular function ( co-MF ) or cellular component ( co-CC ) [25] , shared gene knockout phenotype ( co-Pheno ) [18] or shared protein domain assignment ( co-Interpro ) [18] .
abstract_sentence: Reasoning methods enhance the extracted knowledge by identifying relationships, such as two genes sharing an ontology term or database entry.

fact: Reasoning is also used to combine all sources into a knowledge network that represents the integration of all sorts of relationships between a pair of genes, and to calculate a combined reliability score.
source_span: Reasoning methods enrich the knowledge that results from reading by , for example , noting two genes that are annotated to the same ontology term or database entry . Reasoning is also used to combine all sources into a knowledge network that represents the integration of all sorts of relationships between a pair of genes , and to calculate a combined reliability score . abstract_sentence: Reasoning also combines all sources into a knowledge network, representing relationships between gene pairs, and calculates a combined reliability score.

fact: The orthomyxovirus Thogoto virus (THOV) ML protein regulates immune responses by engaging general transcription factor TFIIB.
source_span: Here , we propose a yet uncharacterized mechanism of immune regulation by the orthomyxovirus Thogoto virus ( THOV ) ML protein through engaging general transcription factor TFIIB . However , we identified two interactors that were highly significantly enriched in ML samples: the general transcription factor IIB ( TFIIB ) and the largely uncharacterized CAPN15 , a member of the calpain family of proteases ( Figs 1A and S1A ) . We validated ML-specific binding of GST-tagged M and ML to FLAG-tagged CAPN15 and TFIIB ( Fig 1C ) .
abstract_sentence: The orthomyxovirus Thogoto virus (THOV) ML protein regulates immune responses by engaging general transcription factor TFIIB.

fact: The THOV ML protein generates a TFIIB-depleted nuclear environment by relocating TFIIB into the cytoplasm.
source_span: ML generates a TFIIB depleted nuclear environment by re-localizing it into the cytoplasm . Rather, ML generates a TFIIB depleted environment in the nuclei of infected cells by re-localizing TFIIB into the cytoplasm.

fact: In Thogoto virus (THOV) infected cells, the ML protein causes TFIIB to re-localize from the nucleus to the cytoplasm.
source_span: Surprisingly , rTHOV-wt infected cells showed a dramatic re-localization of TFIIB from the nucleus into the cytoplasm ( Fig 2A ) . This re-localization was specific to the ability of ML to bind TFIIB, since infection with recombinant THOVs that expressed ML variants with impaired TFIIB binding , such as rTHOV-ΔML and rTHOV-SW , resulted in nuclear TFIIB localization ( Fig 2A ) .
abstract_sentence: The THOV ML protein generates a TFIIB-depleted nuclear environment by relocating TFIIB into the cytoplasm.

fact: Despite TFIIB depletion, ML expression or TFIIB depletion only alters the expression of a limited number of genes.
source_span: Although a broad effect on gene expression would be anticipated , ML expression , delivery of an ML-derived functional domain or experimental depletion of TFIIB only leads to altered expression of a limited number of genes . Whole transcriptome analysis using next generation sequencing of cells infected with rTHOV-wt revealed only 63 significantly changed genes ( q<0 . 05; fold change ≥2 ) ( Fig 3C , x-axis , green and orange dots , S3 Table ) From these experiments we concluded that ML represses dynamic changes in gene expression , but this inhibitory effect is limited to the activity and regulation of selected promoters .

fact: TFIIB is critically important for the de novo recruitment of RNA polymerase II (Pol II) to promoter start sites.
source_span: Our data indicate that TFIIB is critically important for the de novo recruitment of Pol II to promoter start sites and that TFIIB may not be required for regulated gene expression from paused promoters . TFIID nucleates PIC assembly by binding promoter sequences through its TATA binding protein ( TBP subunit ) [4] and recruits TFIIB , which mediates the association of Pol II with the promoter [5] . The diverse behaviour of signalling components and inflammatory cytokines in respect to TFIIB knockdown ( Fig 5B–5E ) further suggested de novo Pol II recruitment as the main discriminating feature of the affected genes .
abstract_sentence: TFIIB is critically important for the de novo recruitment of RNA polymerase II (Pol II) to promoter start sites.

fact: TFIIB may not be required for regulated gene expression from paused promoters.

The fact that EGF targets were not regulated by TFIIB depletion ( Figs 4D and 5E ) could be attributed to their regulation by polymerase pausing [46] , which potentially does not require TFIIB .

fact: Targeting TFIIB by THOV is a mechanism to affect immune responses while keeping other cellular transcriptional activities intact.
source_span: Since many immune genes require de novo recruitment of Pol II , targeting of TFIIB by THOV represents a neat mechanism to affect immune responses while keeping other cellular transcriptional activities intact . Here, we identified a mechanism that involves viral targeting of a single general transcription factor, TFIIB, and allows perturbance of the innate immune system at a broad scale with minimal influence on other ongoing transcriptional processes. While TFIIB is a general transcription factor and considered to be essential for the transcription of all known genes [5], wt THOV infection did not affect transcription of the majority of genes but showed prominent inhibition of IFN and ISG expression.
abstract_sentence: Targeting TFIIB by THOV is a mechanism to affect immune responses while keeping other cellular transcriptional activities intact.

fact: Interference with TFIIB activity may be a favorable site for therapeutic intervention to control undesirable inflammation.
source_span: Thus , interference with TFIIB activity may be a favourable site for therapeutic intervention to control undesirable inflammation . Importantly , modulation of TFIIB activity provides an exciting opportunity to therapeutically control selected gene expression without massively affecting global transcription . Employment of miniML may allow therapeutic taming of overshooting immune responses and could therefore be beneficial to treat diverse immunopathologies , such as septic shock , specific pathogen-induced immunopathologies , autoimmunity as well as antiviral immunity .
abstract_sentence: Interference with TFIIB activity may be a favorable site for therapeutic intervention to control undesirable inflammation.

fact: Fitness cost was quantified as the ratio between transmission rates of hosts infected by drug-resistant strains and transmission rates of hosts infected by drug-sensitive strains.
source_span: This allows quantification of fitness cost as the ratio between transmission rates of hosts infected by drug resistant strains and transmission rates of hosts infected by drug sensitive strains . For each resistance mutation we quantify the between-host fitness cost as the ratio rλ of the transmission rate of the drug resistant strains divided by the transmission rate of the drug sensitive strain . Hence , rλ < 1 implies that there is a fitness cost associated with a resistance mutation . On the other hand rλ > 1 suggests that the resistance mutation confers an advantage to the viral strain .

fact: The majority of these alleles were effectively neutral and segregating at high frequency in Neanderthals, but became selected against after entering human populations of much larger effective size.
source_span: We propose that the majority of these alleles were effectively neutral—and segregating at high frequency—in Neanderthals , but became selected against after entering human populations of much larger effective size. This suggests that weakly deleterious exonic alleles may have been effectively neutral and drifted up in frequency in Neanderthals [28–30] , only to be slowly selected against after introgressing into modern human populations of larger effective size . However , these alleles started to be purged , by weak purifying selection , after introgressing into the human population , due to its larger effective population size .

fact: Individually, these alleles had a small effect but potentially imposed a heavy genetic load on early-generation human-Neanderthal hybrids.
source_span: While individually of small effect , these alleles potentially imposed a heavy genetic load on the early-generation human–Neanderthal hybrids. Although selection against each deleterious Neanderthal allele is weak , the early-generation human–Neanderthal hybrids might have suffered a substantial genetic load due to the sheer number of such alleles . If , for instance , the interaction was multiplicative , then an average F1 individual would have experienced a reduction in fitness of 1 − ( 1 − 4 × 10−4 ) 7000 ≈ 94% compared to modern humans , who lack all but roughly one hundred of these deleterious alleles .
abstract_sentence: While individually of small effect, these alleles potentially imposed a heavy genetic load on the early-generation human–Neanderthal hybrids.

fact: Differences in effective population size may play a more important role in shaping levels of introgression than previously thought.
source_span: This work suggests that differences in effective population size may play a far more important role in shaping levels of introgression than previously thought. More generally , our results suggest that differences in effective population size and nearly neutral dynamics may be an important determinant of levels of introgression across species and along the genome . Therefore , differences in effective population size between Neanderthals and modern humans , and hence in the efficacy of selection , might well explain observed patterns of introgression on the X as well as on the autosomes .

fact: The study investigates the folding and binding of the pKID domain of CREB to the KIX domain of the co-activator CBP.
source_span: Here , we study the folding and binding of the pKID domain of CREB to the KIX domain of the co-activator CBP . The transcription factor cAMP response-element binding protein ( CREB ) represents a well-characterized paradigm for an unstructured peptide that adopts a folded structure upon binding its co-activator CREB binding protein ( CBP ) [1] , [8] . The phosphorylated KID domain ( pKID ) promotes the recruitment of the transcriptional co-activator CBP ( and the related molecule p300 ) by binding to its kinase-induced domain interacting domain ( KIX ) [12] , [19] .

fact: The binding transition state for pKID and KIX resembles the unstructured state in solution, suggesting CREB becomes structured only after committing to binding.
source_span: From transition-path and Φ-value analyses , we find that the binding transition state resembles the unstructured state in solution , implying that CREB becomes structured only after committing to binding . The main conclusion , of both the experimental study and our simulation study , is that pKID becomes structured only after committing to binding . Our simulations show that the TS structures of this coupled binding-and-folding reaction are more closely related to the unstructured conformations of pKID than to the bound conformation .

fact: The mechanism where structure changes after binding is similar to an induced-fit mechanism.
source_span: A change of structure following binding is reminiscent of an induced-fit mechanism and contrasts with models in which binding occurs to pre-structured conformations that exist in the unbound state at equilibrium . Our analysis of the transition states shows that structure is formed only after binding , which makes pKID binding to KIX more consistent with an induced-fit interpretation , with the interesting difference that here it is the ligand that changes conformation . These findings are in contrast to models that invoke the binding of pre-folded conformations or a TS similar to the complex structure .
abstract_sentence: A change of structure following binding is reminiscent of an induced-fit mechanism and contrasts with models in which binding occurs to pre-structured conformations that exist in the unbound state at equilibrium.

fact: Increasing the amount of structure in the unbound pKID reduces the rate of binding, suggesting a 'fly-casting'-like process.
source_span: Interestingly , increasing the amount of structure in the unbound pKID reduces the rate of binding , suggesting a “fly-casting”-like process . Surprisingly , simulations in which the helical propensity of the unbound pKID was increased resulted in a decrease in the rate of binding in comparison to the unstructured pKID . In fact , we find the opposite to be true: increasing the amount of structure in the unbound pKID slightly reduces the on rate . This slow-down can be understood in the context of the so called “fly-casting” mechanism [32] , in which the increased “capture radius” of an unfolded polypeptide enhances the rate of target binding relative to that of compact folded proteins . While the acceleration that we observe , a factor of ∼1 . 6 , would probably not provide a significant advantage biologically , it demonstrates that being unstructured is certainly not a disadvantage from the point of view of binding rate .

fact: The study demonstrates that the requirements of membrane excitability and a unique resting potential directly constrain sodium channel properties.
source_span: We demonstrate that the simplest theoretical constraints bounding sodium channel diversity—the requirements of membrane excitability and the uniqueness of the resting potential—act directly on constraining sodium channel properties . Finally , we demonstrate that polyclonal neutralizing antibodies produced using the DNA vaccine/goose platform administered post-exposure are capable of preventing disease in the ANDV/Syrian hamster model of lethal HPS . This candidate product has potent anti-viral neutralizing activity and is effective at preventing disease when administered as a post-exposure prophylactic in the Syrian hamster model .
abstract_sentence: These findings demonstrate that the DNA vaccine/goose platform can be used to produce a candidate antiviral biological product capable of preventing a lethal disease when administered post-exposure.

fact: New drugs are needed for Chagas disease because current medicines have toxic effects, partial efficacy, and only target the acute phase.
source_span: The development of new drugs against Chagas disease is a priority since the currently available medicines have toxic effects , partial efficacy and are targeted against the acute phase of disease . The two available drugs used to fight T . cruzi parasites during the acute stage are benznidazole ( BZN ) ( Rochagan , Hoffmann-LaRoche ) and nifurtimox ( Lampit , Bayer ) . These drugs have toxic side effects and are not always effective .

fact: NT1 has a trypanostatic effect, meaning it inhibits parasite growth without killing, while PCH1 specifically affects parasite division.
source_span: NT1 has a trypanostatic effect , while PCH1 affects parasite division . Upon treatment with PCH1 , the morphology of parasites was severely affected ( Fig . 4C ) . We observed larger amastigotes containing multiple nuclei and kinetoplasts , which were disorganized and had lost their normal 3-dimensional relationship . These results suggest that PCH1 induces a defect in cell division . Treatment with NT1 resulted in infected cells containing only a few amastigotes of average size with apparently normal nucleus and kinetoplast ( Fig . 4D ) , suggesting that this compound interferes with proliferation of amastigotes without affecting their morphology .

fact: The prevalence of Opisthorchis viverrini among 3,371 study participants with complete data was 61.1%.
source_span: The prevalence of O . viverrini among 3 , 371 study participants with complete data records was 61 . 1% . The overall prevalence of O . viverrini infection was 61 . 1% ( 95% confidence interval ( CI ) : 59 . 5–62 . 8% ) with a range from 0% to 95 . 1% at the unit of the village . Microscopic examination of duplicate Kato-Katz thick smears derived from a single stool sample revealed a prevalence of O . viverrini of over 60% in a random sample of more than 3 , 000 individuals from 51 villages confirming the high endemicity of this liver fluke infection in Champasack province , southern Lao PDR .

fact: Geostatistical models identified age, Lao Loum ethnic group, educational attainment, specific occupations (rice farmer, fisherman, animal breeder), and unsafe drinking water sources as risk factors for Opisthorchis viverrini infection.
source_span: Geostatistical models identified age , Lao Loum ethnic group , educational attainment , occupation ( i . e . , rice farmer , fisherman , and animal breeder ) , and unsafe drinking water source as risk factors for infection . The risk of infection increased with age , higher educational attainment ( i . e . , secondary schooling and above ) , rural occupation ( rice farmer , fisherman , and animal breeder ) , use of unsafe drinking water , and ethnicity ( Lao Loum were at higher risk of infection ) .
abstract_sentence: Geostatistical models identified age, Lao Loum ethnic group, educational attainment, occupation (i.e., rice farmer, fisherman, and animal breeder), and unsafe drinking water source as risk factors for infection.

fact: A history of praziquantel treatment, access to sanitation, and living further from freshwater bodies were identified as protective factors against Opisthorchis viverrini infection.
source_span: History of praziquantel treatment , access to sanitation , and distance to freshwater bodies were found to be protective factors . On the other hand , access to sanitation , living further away from large freshwater bodies , and history of praziquantel treatment were found to be protective factors . The only significant environmental parameter was distance to freshwater bodies , with a 20% risk reduction for each additional km away from large water bodies ( OR = 0 . 80 , 95% CI: 0 . 67–0 . 97 ) .
abstract_sentence: History of praziquantel treatment, access to sanitation, and distance to freshwater bodies were found to be protective factors.

fact: The spatial patterns of Opisthorchis viverrini infection were primarily determined by environmental factors, with predictive modeling showing low risk in mountainous areas and high risk in the Mekong corridor.
source_span: Spatial patterns of O . viverrini were mainly governed by environmental factors with predictive modeling identifying two different risk profiles: low risk of O . viverrini in the mountains and high risk in the Mekong corridor . The dramatic drop of the range and the strong reduction of village-specific variance ( sigma ) after introduction of environmental covariates both indicate that environmental factors account for most of the spatial correlation .
abstract_sentence: Spatial patterns of O. viverrini were mainly governed by environmental factors with predictive modeling identifying two different risk profiles: low risk of O. viverrini in the mountains and high risk in the Mekong corridor.
